posts.name: dpt
posts.cooked:
arenson9:

I will admit, however, that I don't have all the equipment I'd need. I'd need a balaclava and probably better goggles than my old ski googles which have lost some of their lining. I doubt I'll have those in hand by Tue.

A balaclava is really useful, mainly for going under your helmet. If you don't have a balaclava, I recommend a scarf to cover your face and something to cover your helmet (even a plastic bag). Hands and feet are the other major concerns. Hands you probably know about, but some foot coverings over your shoes are helpful (depending a little on your shoes). You can use plastic bags for that, too. I also wear a long, wicking polyster undershirt and warm leggings in weather like that.

 

I'm pleased to see icebike.org seems to have been resurrected. That will tell you how to prepare for temperatures all the way down to Antarctica.
